title: The Louvre Now ~$36 for Tourists. The Great Wall? ~$5 | China Travel Expert
description:
The Louvre just made itself one of Europe's priciest big museums for foreign visitors — and the gap with China's most famous monument is wild.

Since January 14, 2026 the Louvre charges most non-EU/EEA tourists €32 (up 45% from €22) — about $36 at today's rate. A Great Wall ticket, by contrast, is in its off-season window right now: the Mutianyu entrance drops to ¥35 from November 1 to March 31 — about $5. Same week, and the wall that runs for thousands of kilometres costs more than six times less to walk onto than one museum in Paris.

🧭 Expert Tip: the Great Wall has a low season — entrance fees at the main sections drop from November 1 through late March, so winter is both cheaper and far less crowded (dress warm).

卢浮宫 2026 年 1 月起对非欧盟游客涨到 €32（约 $36）；长城淡季票 11 月起约 ¥35（约 $5）——同一周，便宜六倍多。
